newsitem.title: UK: Medusa plans April placing at around 50 pence/shr.
newsitem.headline: Medusa plans April placing at around 50 pence/shr.

text.p: Medusa Petroleum Plc, the UK oil exploration company which aims to strike it rich in central Europe, said it plans to raise about eight million stg through a placing at probably around 50 pence per share.
The company, founded in 1992, expects share trading on the Alternative Investment Market to start early in April.
Medusa, which is expected to have a market capitalisation of about 13 million stg, said the placing's proceeds will meet its working capital requirement until well into 1999.
Medusa was founded by Michael Seymour, the geologist who earlier started Teredo Petroleum, which was taken over by Cairn Energy Plc in 1993.

Seymour, now Medusa' managing director, has spent the last couple of years investigating the potential of oil fields in Poland and the Czech Republic, where he has built up licences, concessions and the necessary government contacts.

Some of the oil majors are also becoming involved in central Europe. Texaco Inc is busy in Poland, Mobil Corp and Occidental Petroleum Corp in Hungary, while Enterprise Oil Plc is active in Bulgaria and Romania, Seymour said.
"They are getting in, but they are quite slow, while we have got ourselves a foothold," he said.

At the beginning of the century Poland was the sixth largest world oil producer, but the industry in central Europe in general has been lacking investments in up-to-date technology to develop its reserves, Seymour told Reuters.

"What we're planning to do is bring in our expertise and we will develop the fields with modern technology," Seymour said. In Poland, Medusa has an area under concession with the size of 16 average North Sea fields. It will start seismic research there this year and hopes to start drilling in 1999.

Medusa begins drilling in June this year in the Czech Republic. Here it will merge its operations with those of Ireland's Tullow Oil Plc, which will wants to free capacity to develop its operations in the Indian subcontinent and Africa, Seymour said.
Tullow will take up about one million stg in the share placing to end up with a stake of about 25 percent in Medusa.
Production in the Czech Republic could come onstream early in 1998 if everything goes according to plan.
"We have several other areas under review in central Europe which at the moment are still being negotiated," said Seymour.
In the meantime, Medusa will drill two relatively low risk gas wells in Spain.
The wells will be in areas where gas is already produced and Medusa aims to improve flow rates by using modern technology so that at least one well can be on production early in 1998, Seymour said.
